label: first-occurrence m/r/j/p/y/k/a mid-original in sequences starting with w/v/s/l/n/c/x/u/i
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (98.5% of mass). It fires on the first occurrence of a particular group of input tokens (m strongest, then r, j, p, then y, k, a, 0), mostly at positions t=3..6. It never fires at t=0-1, at the delimiter, or meaningfully during copy. Whether it fires depends heavily on the earlier context: it is much more likely when the sequence starts with w, v, s, l, n, c, x, u or i (about 4-5x lift for w and v), and precision goes up further when orig(1) is also in that set (0.75 dev precision when both orig(0) and orig(1) are). The largest activations are on m after a prefix such as w/v/s tokens. It fires less on repeated tokens (in_first=0) and on late positions (t>=7). The trigger-token set and the prefix set are both fuzzy, so precision and recall stay incomplete (dev F1 about 0.47, mass recall 0.69). It looks like a hidden-state-dependent response, not a clean token or position detector.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=2: m, r, j, p; t=3: m, r, j, p; t=6: m, r, j, p) and the first original token (most: w, v, s, l, n, c; least: 0, r, y, p); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=4 & t=3, L=6 & t=5.
